name: Fairmont Empress
insider_take: This iconic château-style castle has reigned over Victoria's Inner Harbour since 1908, welcoming royalty, celebrities, and dignitaries while becoming synonymous with the city's refined British Columbia charm.
whats_special: The Fairmont Empress is famous for creating the legendary afternoon tea tradition in Victoria, served in the ornate Tea Lobby since 1908. The hotel's stunning ivy-covered façade has made it one of Canada's most photographed landmarks, while its position directly on the Inner Harbour offers unparalleled waterfront views of the Parliament Buildings and Belleville Street.
pro_tip: Book afternoon tea at least 2-3 weeks in advance, especially during summer months. Request a harbour-view room on higher floors for spectacular sunrise views over the Inner Harbour and Olympic Mountains.
dont_miss: The hotel's famous afternoon tea service in the Tea Lobby, strolling through the beautifully maintained gardens, and watching the sunset from the harbour-side terrace. The Royal BC Museum and Thunderbird Park are just a 3-minute walk away, while whale watching tours depart directly from the adjacent Inner Harbour.
pros: Iconic Landmark Property — A National Historic Site dating to 1908, the Fairmont Empress is one of Canada's most celebrated grand hotels, offering unmatched architectural beauty and heritage charm on Victoria's Inner Harbour.

World-Famous Afternoon Tea — The hotel's legendary Afternoon Tea service is a bucket-list experience, drawing guests from around the globe for its signature blends, freshly baked scones, and elegant Victorian-inspired presentation.

Unbeatable Waterfront Location — Situated directly on Victoria's picturesque Inner Harbour, guests enjoy stunning water views, walkable access to top attractions, shops, and the city's vibrant cultural scene.

Luxurious Fairmont Gold Experience — The exclusive Fairmont Gold floor offers elevated amenities including a private lounge, dedicated concierge service, curated culinary offerings, and enhanced room finishes for a truly refined stay.

Exceptional Dining & Wellness Offerings — From the acclaimed Q at the Empress restaurant featuring Pacific Northwest cuisine to the Willow Stream Spa, guests are treated to a full suite of on-site indulgences without ever leaving the property.
cons: Historic Building Constraints — As a cherished heritage property, some rooms reflect the architectural character of the era with smaller footprints and varying layouts, which may not suit guests expecting uniformly modern, spacious accommodations.

Island Destination — Victoria is located on Vancouver Island and requires a ferry crossing or float plane journey from the mainland, adding travel time and planning considerations for guests flying into Vancouver.

Premium Pricing Reflects Iconic Status — As one of Canada's most storied luxury hotels, rates and on-site experiences (including Afternoon Tea) are priced at a premium, making it best suited for special occasion or aspirational travel.
